BPMN.space / team project

BPMN.space

A useful diagram starts with the right question.

This team-built hackathon prototype helps analysts turn documents and notes into an editable process map, keeping questions, assumptions and sources visible beside it.

Explore the example ↓
My contribution

Member of the development team

Status

Team prototype

Tools

Python · FastAPI · Pydantic · PostgreSQL · React · TypeScript

The document does not say everything

A procedure may describe activities in detail yet omit who approves a request. Conditions can be ambiguous, transitions missing and documents contradictory. Turning that text straight into a polished diagram can make gaps look like established facts. We built BPMN.space around a different workflow: collect sources, expose uncertainty, clarify it with an analyst, then discuss the resulting model. A convincing picture alone does not solve the analysis problem.

Questions belong in the workspace

With a teammate, I contributed to a project that connects documents, questions and diagram versions. An analyst’s answer becomes a new source that can be related to the question. Receiving an answer is not the same as resolving uncertainty: its evidence must address the relevant condition and provide enough information. The capabilities described in this case are team outcomes, combining architecture, interface work and interaction with a generative model.

The model proposes; code constructs

Generation is split into stages. A model proposes a typed graph in JSON. Code checks its connections and supported constructs, compiles BPMN XML and passes the result to layout and technical checks. The intermediate representation narrows the possible errors and supports specific feedback. The trade-off is an explicit boundary: generation supports a defined BPMN subset rather than every feature of the standard. The editor’s palette may support more than automatic generation.

Manual work should survive another run

An analyst can edit the diagram and revisit earlier versions. Subsequent generation needs to respect that work, while a conflict with a new source should become a visible question. The project provides priority for manual changes and a separate rebuild-from-sources operation. This creates a clear division of responsibility: the system proposes and checks, while the person refines meaning. Valid XML is one level of correctness; an accurate business process still depends on evidence and judgement.

What the prototype demonstrates

The graph model and deterministic XML compilation are implemented, within a workflow connecting source material, questions and diagram editing. The prototype provides a basis for discussion, without proving accuracy on arbitrary procedures or measured time savings. Participation in the hackathon does not imply adoption by its organiser. The fictional purchasing example on this page turns a missing approver into a question, connects an answer to evidence, and updates the diagram. It illustrates the principle rather than connecting to the live service.

A useful AI tool helps reveal what we do not know before turning it into a decision.
